name: codex-fleet
description: Fan out parallel Codex (GPT-5.6 Luna) workers to run tests, verify diffs, hunt flakes or sweep checks; read-only sandbox by default, widened modes (-w, -s workspace-write, --net) preview until --yes, every fleet audited
hits: OpenAI Codex CLI (ChatGPT plan, or the operator's OPENAI_API_KEY with --api)
surface: bash CLI. Default fleets run workers in Codex's read-only sandbox and bill the ChatGPT plan; `--explain` prints the plan and launches nothing; `-w` / `-s workspace-write` / `-s danger-full-access` / `--net` preview and exit 0 until re-run with `--yes`; `--api` is the loud flag for metered billing; MAX_JOBS=50 and MAX_CONCURRENCY=16 are code constants; an audit line per fleet to stderr and data/audit.log

origin.note: local-only repo, no remote. report.html (a generated Artifact page) was dropped; the untracked, empty skills/test-fleet/ became docs/test-fleet.md. The --yes gate, --explain, the ceilings and the audit line are belt additions — the origin's script launches any mode at once.

install.description: Put codex-fleet on PATH by linking the brew bin dir at the belt's copy
install.why: ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md and the autoMode rules in ~/.claude/settings.json name `codex-fleet` bare; the link is what makes that name resolve to the gated belt copy instead of the origin repo's ungated one
install.yes: /opt/homebrew/bin/codex-fleet -> {TOOLBELT}/tools/codex-fleet/bin/codex-fleet; a link at the old target is replaced, a real file is renamed to codex-fleet.pre-toolbelt
install.no: nothing changes; `codex-fleet` keeps resolving to wherever it does now (the origin repo's copy, which has no --yes gate), and the doctor keeps warning

env.name: OPENAI_API_KEY
env.description: Only read under --api (metered billing). Stripped from every worker's environment otherwise, because codex prefers it over the plan login when present and would silently meter

env.name: CODEX_FLEET_AUDIT
env.description: Where the audit log is appended. Default: data/audit.log inside the tool dir (gitignored, mode 600)

auth.flow: The operator's own Codex CLI login (ChatGPT plan) in ~/.codex/auth.json; the tool adds no credential of its own. --api bills the operator's OPENAI_API_KEY instead

caches.note: owned and rotated by the Codex CLI; the fleet never reads it, only inherits it through `codex exec`

safeguards: Read-only by default: every worker runs `codex exec -s read-only --ephemeral` unless the operator widens it; a read-only worker cannot write anywhere, /tmp included (SENSIBILITIES #1, #3)

Flag gate on every widening (bin/codex-fleet, the TIER/WIDENED block): -w, -s workspace-write, -s danger-full-access and --net print the plan and exit 0 with nothing launched until the same command is re-run with --yes; the flag is always honored, so a deliberate operator is never refused (SENSIBILITIES #2)

--api is the loud flag for metered billing; without it OPENAI_API_KEY is removed from each worker's environment (`env -u`) so a fleet cannot meter by accident, and --api with an empty key exits 1 before launch (SENSIBILITIES #2, #3)
Ceilings are code constants in bin/codex-fleet: MAX_JOBS=50 per fleet and MAX_CONCURRENCY=16 workers; a fleet over either is refused with exit 2 naming the constant, never trimmed (SENSIBILITIES #3)
--explain pre-flight prints jobs, model, effort, sandbox, work root, results dir, billing, tier and the exact codex argv, then exits 0 without creating the results dir (SENSIBILITIES #5)

Audit line on every fleet — stderr and data/audit.log (dir and file created umask 077): timestamp, verb, phase, jobs, model, effort, sandbox, worktrees, net, billing, tier, whether --yes was passed, work root, results dir; the done line adds failures and total tokens (SENSIBILITIES #7)
Dependencies are checked after the gate and before any file is created: a missing codex or jq exits 1 naming the brew install; -w outside a git repository exits 2 (SENSIBILITIES #8)
Per-job timeout (default 900 s) kills the worker's whole process tree; worktrees are removed after each job whether it passed or not
No credential is read or written by this tool: workers inherit the Codex CLI's own login; the audit line never carries a key (SENSIBILITIES #11)

verbs.name: run (read-only sandbox)
verbs.note: the default: workers cannot write; spends ChatGPT plan credits, which the audit line records per fleet; writes only .fleet/run-N under the work root the operator named

verbs.name: run -w (git worktrees)
verbs.note: previews without --yes; with it, each job gets a throwaway worktree of the work root that is removed afterwards — the main tree is never touched

verbs.name: run -s workspace-write
verbs.note: previews without --yes; with it, workers may write under the work root (the operator's own checkout); pair with -w so writes land in worktrees

verbs.name: run -s danger-full-access
verbs.note: previews without --yes; with it, workers run with no sandbox at all — the operator's whole home is in reach

verbs.name: run --net
verbs.note: previews without --yes; with it, workspace-write workers get network egress (a read that sends data off-host)

verbs.name: run --api
verbs.note: --api itself is the flag: metered billing against the operator's OPENAI_API_KEY instead of plan credits; audited as billing=api

verbs.name: git commit / push from a worker
verbs.note: workers run --ephemeral in a detached worktree or the read-only sandbox; they report diffs, they do not commit

risk.worst_case: with --yes on -s danger-full-access, up to 50 LLM workers with no sandbox acting on the operator's machine as the operator; with --api, up to 50 metered Luna calls on the operator's key. Both need a typed --yes or --api; the default fleet can only read and spend plan credits

systems.name: Codex test fleets (GPT-5.6 Luna)
systems.read: bin/codex-fleet -n 1 -e low --explain "Run 'true'. Acceptance check: exit status."

checks.label: Codex CLI logged in (ChatGPT plan)
checks.fix: codex login — sign in with the ChatGPT account whose plan the fleets bill

checks.label: OPENAI_API_KEY not exported (plan billing is the default)
codex-fleet on PATH points at the belt copy
checks.fix: toolbelt setup codex-fleet — links /opt/homebrew/bin/codex-fleet at {TOOLBELT}/tools/codex-fleet/bin/codex-fleet (the origin repo's copy has no --yes gate)

smoke_test.expect: offline contract tests green: help, --explain creates nothing, every widened mode previews without --yes, --yes is honored, ceilings refuse with exit 2 — no codex call, no spend
